notes: §1985:VI.4.5.2 (printed page VI-13 rendered) prints, after the header, one bracket closed by the paragraph's period: the implementor-name-1 entries (four alternatives of mnemonic-name and ON/OFF STATUS), then ALPHABET, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS and CLASS clauses, each repeatable, then one CURRENCY SIGN IS literal-6 and one DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, and §1985:IV.2.1 fixes the sequence ("Clauses must be written in the sequence given in the general formats."). Implemented at 85: specialNameEntry parses every clause and BindSpecialNames binds them (BindImplementorNameEntry, AlphabetBind, SwitchBindSymbolic, SwitchBindClass, SwitchBindCurrency, SwitchBindDecimalPoint); the four switch alternatives, the five alphabet forms, THROUGH or ALSO as alternatives (COBOL2242), the optional words and the one closing period (ScreenParagraphPeriods, COBOL3407 and COBOL3408) follow the format; the later editions' FOR ALPHANUMERIC and NATIONAL, LOCALE, UTF-8, PICTURE SYMBOL, ORDER TABLE, DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE, CRT STATUS and CURSOR are refused at 85. Five arms are not, each accepted in silence at --std 85: (1) a second CURRENCY SIGN clause, where the 1985 bracket has no ellipsis (SwitchBindCurrency registers every clause and VisitCurrencySignClause gates only PICTURE SYMBOL); both signs then work in PICTURE strings; (2) CLASS ... IN alphabet-name, a phrase the 1985 CLASS clause does not print (§2023:12.3.7.2 added it; VisitClassDefinitionClause gates only the FOR phrase and SwitchBindClass applies the alphabet); (3) DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA written twice, at every edition (no count in SwitchBindDecimalPoint or ClosedFormatPass); (4) the clauses in any order, DECIMAL-POINT before CURRENCY SIGN before CLASS before ALPHABET before a switch entry (the open analysis kb/Work PB1578, raised against 2023); (5) SPECIAL-NAMES followed by two periods and no clause, the 2023 spelling of §2023:12.3.7.3 SR31, where the 1985 bracket gives the second period only with a clause (the defect this pass records on 1985-FMT-VI.4.3.2). The witness writes two ALPHABET clauses, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS with IN, two CLASS clauses, CURRENCY SIGN and DECIMAL-POINT in the printed order and uses each. Probed at --std 85 (67 programs): refused are a bare switch-name, ON STATUS twice, an unknown implementor-name, ALPHABET without the word, STANDARD-1 followed by a literal, THRU after ALSO, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS with no integer, with unequal counts, or continued after its IN phrase, CLASS with no literal, CURRENCY with no literal, DECIMAL-POINT IS PERIOD, a period between clauses and a missing final period.

next.reason: Amendment 1 (X3.23a-1989, its change for page VI-13 (T): 'Paragraph 4.5.2, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS clause, delete outermost set of braces') corrected a typographical error only; the paragraph's syntax is what it was. §1985:VI.4.5.2 has implementor-name-1 with a mnemonic-name and ON/OFF STATUS, ALPHABET (STANDARD-1, STANDARD-2, NATIVE, implementor-name-2, literals), SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, CLASS, one currency clause ('SIGN IS literal-6') and DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA. §2023:12.3.7.2 keeps each: implementor-name-1 as switch-name-1, feature-name-1 or device-name-1 ('The implementor shall specify the names that are available for switch-name-1, feature-name-1, and device-name-1', §2023:12.3.7.3 SR8), implementor-name-2 as code-name-1 ('The implementor shall specify the names supported for code-name-1 and code-name-2', §2023:12.3.7.3 SR15), and the 1985 outer bracket around the clauses and their final period as 'One of the separator periods may be omitted if none of the clauses in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph is specified' (§2023:12.3.7.3 SR31). 2023 accepts paragraphs the 1985 format refuses: a repeatable CURRENCY SIGN with PICTURE SYMBOL, FOR ALPHANUMERIC or NATIONAL on CLASS and SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, IN on CLASS, ALPHABET with LOCALE and FOR NATIONAL, CRT STATUS ('IS data-name-2'), CURSOR, LOCALE ('locale-name-1 IS'), 'dynamic-length-structure-clause' and ORDER TABLE ('ordering-name-1 IS literal-9'). The printed clause order differs as well (1985: implementor-names, ALPHABET, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, CLASS, CURRENCY, DECIMAL-POINT; 2023: 'alphabet-name-clause' first, the switch, feature and device names and 'symbolic-characters-clause' near the end), and each edition binds its own order: 'Clauses must be written in the sequence given in the general formats' (§1985:IV.2.1); 'shall be written in the compilation group in the sequence given in the general format, unless otherwise specified by the rules of that format' (§2023:5.2.1), and no rule of §2023:12.3.7.3 frees it (page 320 of the 2023 PDF, rendered, prints no choice indicators around the clauses). Compile-time on both sides.
